So despite my distaste for the degeneracy that is Lucasarts and company, I decided to watch Solo just so I could view the depths to which they have sunk. Thankfully I was offered the opportunity free of charge as I would never give that horrendous company another cent after the abomination that is the Last Jedi.

I put aside my previous feelings and decided to give the movie a true unbiased review and only judged the movie on its function within the Star Wars Universe.

Funnily enough the first 10 minutes of the movie were surprisingly entertaining. The plight of Han and Qi’ra as well as their escape from Corellia was believable. Their separation as well only serves to further complement the story. However the movie truly took a blaster to the mythos when Han signs up for the Imperial Legion.

I will not accept the notion that the infamous name Han Solo was coined by some Imperial Desk Jockey on the backwards scum planet of Corellia. That is a disgrace to even entertain let alone assert in “canon”.

From there the movie devolves into utter trash. The scene of an imperial battle was initially interesting but after a moronic scene where the Imperial Legion commander refuses to even elucidate the clear objective of their campaign is untenable. The makers of this film are trying to assert that the clean and efficient galaxy conquering machine that was the Empire does not even provide the basic plans to its front line troops is brain melting.

Immediately afterwards we are treated to a scene I refuse to acknowledge. Human vocal cords cannot vibrate at the correct frequency to emulate Shyriiwook.

We are introduced to Expendables 1 through 3. And expendables 1 and 2 expire within the life cycle of a fruit fly. Expendable 3 gifts Han his signature blaster. For which I must admit is a nice touch. Han’s blaster is less of a handgun and more of a sawed off shotgun.

Sadly the rest of the movie is as predictably rushed and boring as can be. Donald Glover, Lando is not. SJW bot was actually a perfect representation and fitting for this film. NPCs on the internet. Programmable Droids in real life. Expendable 3 is retired by Han as it should be.

The visuals of the film echo the inconsequential nature of this film save for one scene. The entire sequence with the Millenium falcon struggling to escape a gravity well while being pursued by a planet sized squid was gorgeous in comparison to the rest of the film.

Nothing else of note happens except for the surprise appearance of one very bad impersonator.

I’m unable to understand how they made a 6 foot tall demon faced Sith Lord seem less intimidating than a 12 year old in a helmet. In his last film appearance Darth Maul radiated power and ferociousness. Here he feels more like a petulant child who has a taste for blood. Even King Joffery was more sinister than this representation.

However after the credits rolled I didn’t find myself in a state of turmoil or disgust that I had after the premiere of The Last Jedi or the excitement after The Force Awakens.

No.

Instead I felt an unrelenting pool of sadness bubble up from my imagination. The mythic and legendary Star Wars Universe had been pulled out of the ephemera. The magic that made this stupid but incredible story of space wizards and aliens had disappeared like the ticket sales to the movie. Somehow they made Han Solo’s origin within the vast universe one thing Star Wars could never be.

Forgettable.

The Last Jedi may have cut Star Wars in half, but Solo buried any Hope of a Return.

If only they had buried Darth Maul and this entire story instead.
Strangely enough, I also watched Solo last night for the first time.

Step 1: Head on over to Wookieepedia.

Step 2: Click that button that says "Legends"

Presto! Star Wars is good again!
